One may wish to be like another only in two cases: one given wealth who spends it rightly, and one given wisdom who acts on it and teaches it.
One may wish to be like only two men: one given the Quran who recites it night and day, and one given wealth who spends it rightly.
None should wish for death over a calamity, but ask to live while life is better; only the ban kept Khabbab from wishing it, and deeds alone earn none Paradise.
Khabbab, branded seven times, would have prayed for death but for the Prophet's ban; none should long for death over a calamity but ask to live while life is better.
Unable to sleep, the Prophet wished a righteous companion would guard him and Sa'd came, while Bilal longed to spend a night in a Meccan valley.
The Prophet forbade longing for or praying for death, for a good person may do more good and an evildoer may repent; Anas and Khabbab held back.
Do not long to meet the enemy, but ask Allah for safety.
One may wish only to be like two men: one given the Quran who recites it night and day, and one given wealth who spends it rightly.
